newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Celsius sees 1996 profit of 275 mln SKR.
newsitem.headline: Celsius sees 1996 profit of 275 mln SKR.

text.p: Swedish defence industries group Celsius AB on Thursday forecast its profits after financial items for calendar 1996 would reach 275 million crowns.
This compared to a loss of 559 million crowns in 1995.

"Development so far indicates 1996 will be a relatively decent year for the Celsius group despite a weakening defence market," Celsius managing director Olle Lund said in the company's nine-month results statement.
"The forecast for the year points to a level of 275 million crowns thanks above all to a very strong financial net."

Celsius posted a 36 percent jump in profit to 202 million crowns after financial items for the first nine months of 1996 compared to the same 1995 period. Sales fell to 7.71 billion crowns from 8.07 billion.
Lund said changes within its business operations should result in a better profit in 1997.

"The capacity adjustment now taking place in the defence-related operations should lead to a positive development for the group in the future, and therefore for that reason I estimate the operating profit for the coming year will improve," he said.

Celsius blamed uncertain demand from the Swedish defence forces for lower sales but said that for some units order intake and turnover rose because of export possibilities and an increased proportion of civilian orders.
"The year has been characterised by signficant uncertainty about the overall future needs of the Swedish defence industry," it said.
"This has meant that domestic order intake has been relatively weak for several divisions within the Celsius group."

Bofors, which manufactures army, navy and air force weapons systems, posted sales of 2.84 billion crowns, a rise from 2.74 billion, helped by orders from the Swedish Defence Material Administration, Austria and the U.S. Army.
Submarine and surface vessel unit Kockum's sales fell 11 percent to 1.86 billion crowns.

Order intake of CelsiusTech, which develops electronics systems for defence and non-military use, rose slightly, to 1.28 billion crowns in the first nine months of the year from 1.23 billion a year earlier.
